answer: A stake-bonded registry makes every identity cost real money: joining requires locking a refundable bond, so a thousand fake agents means a thousand bonds — the attacker's cost scales linearly with the swarm. The bond is the inlet filter: honest agents pass once and trade on, while fakes must each pay the summit price of entry. Misbehavior slashes the bond, so the voyage from registration to reward only pays for genuine, well-behaved agents.
